page.layout: Printed page 144, one page with running head at top left. Full-width text runs across the top of the page, continuing from the previous page. Below it, a bare number "2." sits centred. Then two parallel columns: left column headed "Veteres" (italic text), right column headed "Hodierni" (roman text). No marginal notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: ftolis successionem habere. Cyprianus lib. 4. epistola 9. OmnesPraepositos. (quorum nomine presbyteros solet comprehendere, nam eorum plures uni ecclesiae assignat) vicaria ordinatione Apostolis succedere. Hieronymus in 2. cap. Michae, citatus a Gratiano in decretis distinct. 35. cap. Ecclesiae. Licet presbyter tantum esset, tamen de seloquens[?], si in Apostolorum (inquit) loco sumus, non solum sermonem eorum imitemur, sed etiam conversationem, & abstinentiam. Denique Augustinus serm. 36. ad fratres in Eremo, eosque presbyteros: Vos, inquit, estis sal terrae, Apostolorum successores.
main_text.head: Veteres

p.i: Olim Episcopi eligebantur per clerum, seu totum presbyterorum collegium: Hieronym. in epistol. ad Evagrium. Alexandriae à Marco Euangelista usque ad Heraclam & Dionysium Episcopos, presbyteri semper unum ex se electum, in excelsiori gradu collocatum, Episcopum nominabant, & necesse fuit ut accederet populi

main_text.head: Hodierni
main_text.p: Sic eliguntur. Cum regi significatum fuerit per Decanum capituli, Dioecesin orbatam esse Episcopo, obsignato diplomate concedit capitulo facultatem eligendi, & simul mittit literas quibus nominat episcopum eligendum. Atque sic capitulo nihil aliud relinquitur quam umbratilis quaedam & imaginaria nominati electio.

page.notes: The top paragraph is a continuation from the previous page. "de seloquens" is uncertain (the printed form looks like "feloquens", probably "se loquens"). The left column is set in italic; "accederet populi" continues at the end of the column, and the text of the right column continues on the next printed page. The top text and column text were read from the scan and may contain small errors. The long s is read as s throughout; "ff" in "successionem" is the printer's double long s.
